A.name: A. NRHO staging (Orion + refilled lander)
notes: Orion needs 1000 m/s (cited sum) of its 1050 m/s: feasible with 50 m/s spare.
Lander holds 1621 t of propellant in LEO of 1600 t tank capacity.

B.name: B. Low lunar orbit staging with Orion
notes: Patched conic, coplanar, no margin: 1643 m/s (LOI 821 + TEI 821).
NASA figure with Artemis design factors (global access, margins): 2800 m/s.
Orion capability: 1050 m/s. Short by 593 m/s even in the ideal case, which is why Artemis stages in NRHO.

C.name: C. Direct crewed ship (no Orion)
notes: Ship holds 2044 t in LEO (incl. 30 t Earth landing reserve) of 1600 t capacity.
Earth entry at about 11 km/s on a Starship heat shield qualified for 7.8 km/s LEO returns: the key new capability; see the entry check.
Lunar ice gives oxygen and hydrogen, not carbon, so methane comes from Earth.
Descent propellant (208 t) is loaded in NRHO; only ascent oxygen (112 t) is made on the Moon; ascent methane (31 t) is landed as cargo.
All oxygen for the next round trip made on the Moon; all methane landed as cargo.
Carrying the next descent's propellant up to NRHO costs more than it saves.
Water splits 8:1 oxygen to hydrogen by mass; at mixture ratio 5.5 hydrogen is the limit and 30 t oxygen is left over.
